title: Kernel of the map to the extended-ideal chart
statement:
Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $a\in I$. Put $b=f(a)$, $J=IB$, and $C=C_a(A,B,I)=B\otimes_A A[I/a]$ as in [def-nagata-strict-transform-basechange-chart-ring]. Let $\sigma_a:C\to B[J/b]\subseteq B_b$ be the homomorphism of [def-nagata-strict-chart-to-extended-blowup-chart], and let $\alpha$ be the structural image of $a$ in $C$. Then
$$\ker(\sigma_a)=\Gamma_{(a)}(C)=\{z\in C\mid \exists n\geq0,\ \alpha^n z=0\},$$
where power torsion has the meaning of [def-nagata-power-torsion] for the $A$-module $C$.

proof.text:
By [def-nagata-strict-transform-basechange-chart-ring], $C=B\otimes_A A[I/a]$ and $a$ acts through its structural image. Write $R=A[I/a]$ and let $\iota:B\to C$ be $y\mapsto y\otimes1$, so $\alpha=\iota(b)$. Fix $z\in C$ and express it as a finite sum $z=\sum_{i=1}^r y_i\otimes c_i$ using the generators and bilinear relations of the tensor product. By [lemma-nagata-chart-ring-normal-form], choose $c_i=x_i/a^{n_i}$ in $A_a$, with $x_i\in I^{n_i}$. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], $R$ is a subalgebra of $A_a$, so $a^{n_i}c_i=x_i$ holds in $R$, not merely after another localization. Put $N=\sum_i n_i$ (zero for an empty sum). Multiplication on pure tensors and the factor maps are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Tensor balancing and distributivity give
$$\alpha^Nz=\sum_i y_i\otimes a^Nc_i
=\sum_i y_i\otimes a^{N-n_i}x_i
=\iota\!\left(\sum_i y_i b^{N-n_i}f(x_i)\right).$$
Denote the displayed element of $B$ by $w$. This calculation uses no injectivity of $B\to C$ and no cancellation of $a$ in $C$.

proof.text:
Suppose $\sigma_a(z)=0$. By [def-nagata-strict-chart-to-extended-blowup-chart], $\sigma_a$ is a $B$-algebra map, hence its composite with $B[J/b]\hookrightarrow B_b$ sends $\iota(w)$ to $w/1$ and $\alpha$ to $b/1$. Applying this composite to the equation of step 1 gives $w/1=(b/1)^N\sigma_a(z)=0$. Apply [lemma-nagata-power-torsion-kernel-localization] to the $B$-module $B$ and the element $b$: there is $m\geq0$ with $b^m w=0$ in $B$. Therefore
$$\alpha^{N+m}z=\alpha^m\iota(w)=\iota(b^m w)=0.$$
By [def-nagata-power-torsion], $z\in\Gamma_{(a)}(C)$.

proof.text: Conversely let $z\in\Gamma_{(a)}(C)$. By [def-nagata-power-torsion], choose $n\geq0$ with $\alpha^nz=0$. The map of [def-nagata-strict-chart-to-extended-blowup-chart] sends this equation, after inclusion into $B_b$, to $(b/1)^n\sigma_a(z)=0$. In $B_b$ the element $b/1$ has inverse $1/b$; multiplying by $(1/b)^n$ gives $\sigma_a(z)=0$ there. Since $B[J/b]$ is literally a subalgebra of $B_b$, equality there detects zero in $B[J/b]$ as well. Thus $z\in\ker(\sigma_a)$. Together with step 2 this is the asserted equality. In particular the argument also applies to the zero localization ring.

blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

proof.text:
Both source and target map to $B_b$. The target $B[J/b]$ is the subalgebra
generated there by the fractions from $J$, and $\sigma_a$ has exactly that
image by [lemma-nagata-strict-chart-map-surjective]. Thus its kernel
is the kernel of localization at $b$. Under the $A$-action this is the
kernel of localization at $a$, which equals the $a$-power torsion by
[lemma-nagata-power-torsion-kernel-localization].
